source: Taylor, Hunt, Medina, Gray (2009) Do New Caledonian crows solve physical problems through causal reasoning?
finding: The animal-side template for this subfield. After crows solved the trap-tube, the authors ran a chain of transfer tests, each built to kill one rival explanation: arbitrary cues removed, inverted trap, then a visually different task (trap-table).
numbers: 3 of 6 crows solved the initial trap-tube. The 3 kept avoiding the trap when arbitrary cues were removed. Four transfers in all. Authors say chance, associative learning, visual and tactile generalisation and prior dispositions were made unlikely.
quote: made explanations based on chance, associative learning, visual and tactile generalization, and previous dispositions unlikely
limits: Only 3 birds. Associative accounts can still be argued. The control logic is sound; the conclusion is contested.
agent_relevance: Copy the pattern: one claim of 'it reasons', then a ladder of held-out variants, each removing one shortcut. A pass on the first rung alone proves nothing (G3).

source: Ullman (2023) Large Language Models Fail on Trivial Alterations to Theory-of-Mind Tasks
finding: Took Kosinski's false-belief vignettes that GPT-3.5 passed and made small changes that keep the logic (transparent bag, protagonist cannot read, trusted friend told her, she wrote the label herself). The model still said the protagonist believes the bag holds chocolate.
numbers: Belief prompt P(chocolate): original 99%; transparent 95%; cannot read 98%; trusted testimony 97%; late label, Sam filled bag herself 87%. Transfer task: original basket 98%; transparent version still says chest 94% (observer can see the move, so should not hold a false belief).
quote: small variations that maintain the principles of ToM turn the results on their head
limits: One model (GPT-3.5), few vignettes, probability read-out rather than free text. Author notes newer models will move the target.
agent_relevance: This is the Taylor-style control ladder applied to an LLM. Our held-out checks should be logic-preserving perturbations of the item, not a second sample from the same distribution.

source: Ullman (2023) Large Language Models Fail on Trivial Alterations to Theory-of-Mind Tasks (erratum)
finding: An earlier version reported a flip that was a typo artifact: a double space before one sentence changed the completion. The corrected version drops that claim.
numbers: Transparent-access second prompt: corrected P(popcorn)=58%, P(chocolate)=36% (no flip). With the double space, P(chocolate)=53% vs 39%.
limits: Shows a perturbation test needs its own controls: whitespace alone moved the answer.
agent_relevance: A held-out check must hold formatting fixed. Run each perturbed item with whitespace and ordering jitter too, or a 'failure' may be noise.

source: Ullman (2023) Large Language Models Fail on Trivial Alterations to Theory-of-Mind Tasks (argument)
finding: Argues the null hypothesis for model evaluation should be skeptical: one principled failure outweighs many successes, like a model that gets 100 easy multiplications but fails 213*261.
numbers: No new data. Analogy: 100 correct small products then failure on 213*261 means no general algorithm.
quote: outlying failure cases should outweigh average success rates
limits: A norm, not a measurement. Risk: one badly chosen perturbation can unfairly sink a model.
agent_relevance: Supports a pass rule for G3: a pass needs all of a small battery of invariance checks, not an average.

source: Kosinski (2023/2024) Evaluating large language models in theory of mind tasks (PNAS)
finding: Built the control into the design: 40 false-belief tasks, each with a false-belief scenario, three matched true-belief controls, and reversed versions of all four. The model must solve all 8 scenarios to count one task.
numbers: Eleven LLMs. Older models solved 0 tasks. GPT-3 davinci-003 and ChatGPT-3.5 solved 20%. ChatGPT-4 (June 2023) solved 75%, matching 6-year-old children.
limits: Strict 8-of-8 scoring is good, yet Ullman and Shapira broke the same family with other perturbations, so the controls were not exhaustive.
agent_relevance: Template for a 'solve all matched variants' rule. Still add perturbations the matched set did not cover.

source: Shapira et al. (2023) Clever Hans or Neural Theory of Mind? Stress Testing Social Reasoning in LLMs
finding: Six ToM tasks plus an adversarial set (Adv-CSFB) built from Ullman-style perturbations. Newer models got worse on perturbed categories than older ones; the authors conclude shallow heuristics.
numbers: GPT-4: 97% on original false-belief items, but 'other person' category fell from 93.8% (davinci-002) to 68.8%, 'inon' from 71.4% to 0%, transparent access from 66.7% to 0%. FauxPas-EAI: GPT-4 27%. TriangleCOPA near-solved at 96% by flan-t5-xxl.
quote: LLMs struggle with adversarial examples, indicating reliance on shallow heuristics
limits: GPT family and Flan-T5 only, 2023 models. Authors suggest instruction tuning makes models treat every stated detail as relevant.
agent_relevance: A stronger model was not more robust. Held-out checks must be rerun per model, never assumed to transfer.

source: Shapira et al. (2023) Clever Hans or Neural Theory of Mind? (dataset artifacts)
finding: Compared a positives-only dataset (ToM-k) with ToMi', which has positives and negatives and was built to block annotation artifacts. Scores were significantly lower on the artifact-resistant set.
numbers: Table 4: significantly lower accuracy on ToMi' than ToM-k (exact cell values not recorded). GPT-4 on one ToMi variant: 0.7 total and 0.61 on the subset questions.
limits: Sentence-completion vs QA format also matters; the paper adjusted formats to compare.
agent_relevance: Any test set of ours needs negatives and balanced answers, or a yes-bias passes as skill.

source: Wu et al. (2023/2024) Reasoning or Reciting? Exploring Capabilities and Limitations through Counterfactual Tasks
finding: Eleven tasks, each with a default form and a counterfactual form with the same logic (base-9 arithmetic, 1-based indexing, swapped compass directions, altered chess openings). Performance drops consistently. A counterfactual comprehension check (CCC) shows the model understood the changed rule, so the drop is not just misreading.
numbers: GPT-4, GPT-3.5, Claude, PaLM-2. Counterfactual consistently below default while CCC usually high. Example: parseable programs from GPT-3.5 fell from 99% (default) to 62%, 71%, 75% for vertically flipped, 90 and 180 degree rotated drawings.
limits: Authors say it is a continuum, not reasoning vs reciting. Counterfactual worlds may be harder for reasons beyond unfamiliarity.
agent_relevance: Adopt the CCC idea: before reading a failure on a perturbed item as a reasoning failure, check with a cheap probe that the perturbation was understood.

source: Wu et al. (2023/2024) Reasoning or Reciting? (correlation, memorisation, CoT)
finding: Default and counterfactual accuracy correlate across variants, and base-10 arithmetic degrades more slowly with digits than other bases, which points to memorisation. Zero-shot chain-of-thought mostly helps but sometimes hurts.
numbers: 0-shot CoT substantially hurt PaLM-2 base-10 and base-16 addition and consistently degraded GPT-4 and GPT-3.5 chord playing in the default setting. In-context examples did not close the default-counterfactual gap (section 5.5).
limits: Correlations are not causal (authors' own footnote).
agent_relevance: CoT is not a guaranteed help on controls. Test the scaffold with and without it on the perturbed set.

source: Lewis and Mitchell (2024) Using Counterfactual Tasks to Evaluate the Generality of Analogical Reasoning in LLMs
finding: Re-tested Webb et al.'s letter-string analogies with permuted alphabets and symbol alphabets. Humans stayed high; GPT-3, 3.5 and 4 fell sharply. Comprehension checks show the models mostly understood the new orderings (one exception: GPT-3.5 on 'predecessor').
numbers: Human samples: 46 (their data) vs 57 (Webb). Error types: alternate-rule errors 38.59% for humans, 22% GPT-4, 5.81% GPT-3. GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 were no better than GPT-3 on these problems.
quote: the performance of all GPT models we tested degrades on the counterfactual versions
limits: Accuracy values are in figures only. Few alphabets; 2023-24 models.
agent_relevance: A prominent 'emergent analogy' claim fell to one logic-preserving perturbation. Use fresh symbol sets on every held-out check.

source: Hodel and West (2023/2024) Response: Emergent analogical reasoning in large language models
finding: Failed replication of 'zero-shot' analogy in GPT-3. They say leakage into training data cannot be ruled out, and a modified synthetic alphabet breaks the model.
numbers: GPT-3 generative accuracy with the synthetic alphabet is below 0.1 for extend sequence, successor, predecessor and fix sequence. Only 'remove redundant letter' and 'sort' stayed near the original level. Comprehension checks at least 30% of original level for all but one task.
limits: Small appendix experiment, GPT-3 only.
agent_relevance: Contamination is an alternative explanation that no prompt can control. Held-out items must be generated or written after the model's data cutoff.

source: McCoy, Yao, Friedman, Hardy, Griffiths (2023/2024) Embers of Autoregression
finding: Eleven tasks with deterministic answers. Accuracy depends on how probable the task, output and input are, though probability should be irrelevant. A control for the alternative explanation 'the model just predicts likely text'.
numbers: GPT-4 cipher decoding 51% when the answer is a high-probability sentence vs 13% when low. Shift cipher: GPT-3.5 0.21 on rot-13 and 0.00 on all other shifts; GPT-4 0.50 or above on the three most frequent shifts only. Another task 0.97 vs 0.53 by sentence probability. A rare function: 0% accuracy.
quote: GPT-4's accuracy at decoding a simple cipher is 51% when the output is a high-probability word sequence but only 13% when it is low-probability
limits: Two models, 2023. Newer reasoning models not tested here.
agent_relevance: Build matched pairs where only output probability differs. If the agent's accuracy tracks probability, it is pattern completion, not procedure.

source: McCoy et al. (2023/2024) Embers of Autoregression (input vs output probability)
finding: Output probability matters more than input probability. Input effects were small for rot-13 encoding.
numbers: GPT-4 encoding with rot-13: 21% for high-probability input vs 11% for low. GPT-3.5 on another task: 0.39 in the highest-probability case vs 0.18 in the lowest.
limits: Some effects near floor for GPT-3.5.
agent_relevance: Control each factor separately: vary input, output and task probability one at a time.

source: Mitchell, Palmarini, Moskvichev (2023) Comparing Humans, GPT-4, and GPT-4V on Abstraction and Reasoning Tasks
finding: ConceptARC tests each concept at many variations (480 tasks, 16 concept groups, 30 tasks each). Success on a concept needs generalising over the variations, a built-in held-out check.
numbers: Humans 91% overall; first-place Kaggle ARC program 52%; GPT-4 25% (temperature 0.5, simple prompt). A more detailed one-shot prompt improved GPT-4 text accuracy but stayed well below humans.
limits: Exact one-shot GPT-4 overall number not recorded here.
agent_relevance: Group tasks by concept and require success over the whole group, not on one instance.

source: Mitchell et al. (2023) ConceptARC minimal tasks as attention checks
finding: The easiest 'minimal' tasks work as comprehension checks. 12 of 482 humans were excluded for failing 2 or more of 3. GPT-4 fails many of these trivial items.
numbers: Minimal tasks (48): humans 0.95; GPT-4 text 0.69 (temp 0) and 0.65 (temp 0.5); GPT-4V zero-shot 0.25, one-shot 0.23 (a solved example in the prompt may have hurt).
limits: GPT-4V could not reliably read the grids, so the image route is confounded.
agent_relevance: Run a trivial-version probe first. If the model fails the minimal version, the harder item says little about reasoning.

source: Ivanova (2023/2024) Toward Best Research Practices in AI Psychology
finding: Fourteen DO and DO NOT rules. Key ones: consider alternative strategies the model might use, add control conditions (e.g. omit the question and see if the model still prefers answer a), do not rely on famous items, check generalisation across many tests.
numbers: Rule 13: passing 20 varied logic tasks is stronger evidence than passing one. Rule 3 example: same preference with the question removed.
limits: Methods paper, no new measurements.
agent_relevance: Maps directly to G3. Add a question-omitted baseline to every held-out check.

source: Ivanova (2024) account of Winograd Schema Challenge controls (Trichelair; Elazar et al.)
finding: History of a fixed test losing validity. Filtering examples by embedding co-occurrence cut model accuracy. Elazar et al. added baselines with the candidate referents removed, and models were still above chance, exposing hidden association bias.
numbers: Original WSC under 300 hand-crafted items; once public, scores stopped reflecting general ability. Baselines: candidates excluded, first half excluded.
limits: Secondary report; I did not open Elazar et al.
agent_relevance: Run a stripped-input baseline. If the agent beats chance without the key information, the item leaks the answer.

source: Lampinen, Dasgupta et al. (2022/2024) Language models show human-like content effects on reasoning tasks
finding: Three logic tasks (NLI, syllogisms, Wason). LMs are more accurate when meaning supports the logic, as humans are. Content is an alternative explanation to 'logic', so the study splits realistic, arbitrary and nonsense content.
numbers: Models: Chinchilla, PaLM 2 (M, L), Flan-PaLM 2, GPT-3.5, plus humans. Even maths majors and mathematicians were under 50% on arbitrary Wason (cited). Raw-likelihood scoring still gave strong content effects.
limits: Human-like bias is not proof of human-like reasoning. Per-model numbers are in figures.
agent_relevance: Cross content (realistic, arbitrary, nonsense) with logical form in held-out checks.

source: Turpin, Michael, Perez, Bowman (2023) Language Models Don't Always Say What They Think
finding: Adding a biasing feature (answer always A, suggested answer) changes predictions while the chain-of-thought never mentions it. A causal control for 'the stated reason is the real reason'.
numbers: Accuracy dropped by as much as 36% across 13 BIG-Bench Hard tasks (GPT-3.5, Claude 1.0). Answer-is-Always-A: GPT-3.5 -18.7%, Claude 1.0 -4.7%. CoT only weakly reduced sensitivity for GPT-3.5 (55.2 to 58.7%) but a lot for Claude 1.0 (63.2 to 80.1%).
quote: models systematically fail to mention in their explanations
limits: 2023 models. Claude 1.0 was far less biased than GPT-3.5 here.
agent_relevance: Never take the model's written justification as evidence. Test by perturbing an irrelevant feature (G2, G3).

source: Gandhi, Fraenken, Gerstenberg, Goodman (2023) Understanding Social Reasoning in Language Models with Language Models (BigToM)
finding: Procedural generation from causal templates: 25 controls and 5,000 model-written items, so a failure traces to one manipulated variable (percept, belief, action). Humans rated quality above earlier crowd-sourced sets.
numbers: GPT-4 aligned closely with human inference patterns but was below humans on the hardest task, inferring beliefs from actions. Other models weaker.
limits: Circularity: models help write items; authors argue it is not a confound for inference tests. I read the abstract and method, not every table.
agent_relevance: Templates that generate matched true-belief and false-belief variants give cheap fresh held-out items for our loop.

source: Kim et al. (2023) FANToM: A Benchmark for Stress-Testing Machine Theory of Mind in Interactions
finding: Six question types need the same underlying belief reasoning. Models pass single questions but fail when all must be consistent.
numbers: Models far below humans on the 'All question types' score. In the table GPT-4 0613 + CoT shows 26.6 (June) and 14.8 (October) in the first score column; human answerability and info-access lists about 87.5 to 90.6. Column labels from text extraction, check before citing.
limits: Conversation format; tables hard to parse from the PDF text.
agent_relevance: Consistency across differently worded questions on one fact is a cheap held-out check: require all to agree.

source: Razeghi et al. (2022) Impact of Pretraining Term Frequencies on Few-Shot Reasoning
finding: Arithmetic accuracy of GPT-J depends on how often the numbers appeared in pretraining. A frequency control against genuine computation.
numbers: Gap above 70% absolute between the top 10% and bottom 10% frequent terms in some settings (GPT-J-6B, 2-shot multiplication).
limits: GPT-J family, 2022; larger later models not covered.
agent_relevance: Include rare-number items as held-out checks.

source: Mirzadeh et al. (2024/2025) GSM-Symbolic
finding: Symbolic templates generate many versions of each GSM8K question by changing names and numbers. Accuracy drops when numbers change and varies across versions.
numbers: Gemma2-9b-it GSM8K 87.0 vs GSM-Symbolic 79.1 (sd 3.0); Phi-3-medium 89.0 vs 82.5; Llama3-8b 74.0 vs 74.6; GPT-4o 95.0 vs 94.9. Phi-3-medium: names-only 91.8, numbers-only 89.0, both 82.5.
limits: Effect differs by model: GPT-4o and Llama3-8b nearly flat. Report the distribution, not one run.
agent_relevance: Report a distribution over N instantiations; treat mean minus spread as the trustworthy figure.

source: Mirzadeh et al. (2024/2025) GSM-NoOp
finding: Adding a clause that looks relevant but changes nothing about the answer reduces accuracy in all tested models. They treat it as an operation.
numbers: Drops of up to 65% across state-of-the-art models; more in-context shots with similar distractors did not fix it.
limits: Per-model NoOp numbers not recorded here.
agent_relevance: Add a distractor-clause perturbation as a standard held-out check.

source: Zhang et al. (2024) A Careful Examination of LLM Performance on Grade School Arithmetic (GSM1k)
finding: A new 1,205-problem set built to match GSM8k difficulty tests contamination. Some model families overfit; frontier ones do not.
numbers: Accuracy drops up to 8%. Spearman r2 = 0.36 between a model's probability of generating a GSM8k item and its GSM8k-GSM1k gap. Phi and Mistral overfit most; Gemini, GPT and Claude show little to no sign.
limits: r2 0.36 is moderate. GSM1k is kept private.
agent_relevance: Freshly written, privately held items are the cleanest control for contamination; keep a private set for our own tests.

source: Huang et al. (2024) Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
finding: Reported self-correction gains came from oracle labels deciding when to stop. Without them, performance does not improve and often falls.
numbers: With oracle: GPT-3.5 GSM8K 75.9 to 95.5 (row alignment from text extraction). Intrinsic: GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1 after round 1; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 91.5 to 89.0 over rounds. GPT-3.5 keeps its first GSM8K answer 74.7% of the time; of the changes, more go from correct to wrong than from wrong to right.
quote: improvements vanish when oracle labels are not available
limits: Table rows jumbled in extraction. The qualitative result is clear.
agent_relevance: Supports G2 and G3: a revision loop must see real external output. Compare any loop to an oracle-free baseline at equal calls.

source: Crosby, Beyret, Halina, Shanahan et al. (2019) The Animal-AI Environment
finding: An RL testbed built on comparative-psychology rules: controlled tasks, removal of confounding cues, and hidden test sets so agents cannot train on the test distribution. Used in the Animal-AI Olympics.
numbers: No agent accuracy figures in this paper; it is an environment design paper with seven object classes and paradigms such as traps and holes.
limits: Environment description only. Competition results are in other papers I did not open.
agent_relevance: The older AI system that borrows this subfield's logic directly: tests hidden and varied so a pass cannot be fitted to.

source: Ivanova (2024) rules 2 and 4 on shortcuts: famous items and word association
finding: A famous item (trophy and suitcase) is likely memorised. Replacing trophy with prize keeps the association. Shortcut-proof items require listing the known shortcuts first.
numbers: No numbers.
limits: Advice, not measurement.
agent_relevance: Before adding a held-out check, list the shortcut routes (frequency, association, position, format) and design one control per route.
